The moving-average stack is in textbook descending order, with **every** average above the price and each above the next:

> **102.35 (close) < 115.11 (10 EMA) < 130.15 (20 SMA / Boll mid) < 160.74 (50 SMA) < 171.84 (200 SMA)**

Historically that magnitude of discount makes a *mean-reversion episode* probable, but it is not, by itself, a timing tool.

**Cumulative drawdown:** −49.1% from the 2026-09-21 close (201.05); −36.3% from the 2026-10-29 close (160.59) in 17 sessions; −63.1% from the 2025-12-09 peak close (277.36).

### 4. The October 30 discontinuity — the single most important structural event

| Date | Close | High | Low | Volume | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-29 | 160.59 | 163.60 | 157.61 | 8.46M | last pre-gap close |
| **2026-10-30** | **143.54** | **148.50** | **136.89** | **20.89M** | gap down ~7.7% at the open; **highest volume in the entire retrieved series** |
| 2026-11-04 | 151.50 | 153.33 | 141.83 | 9.09M | bounce high **153.33 — never reached the 148.50→160.59 gap ceiling… wait, see below** |
| 2026-11-05 | 136.82 | 151.58 | 133.50 | 12.55M | bounce rejected, −9.7%, new low of the move |

Correction for precision: the 11-04 intraday high of 153.33 **did** trade back *into* the gap (gap zone = 148.50 to 160.59), filling roughly 40% of it, and was then sold hard. The gap's **upper edge (160.59) has never been revisited** — 160.59 is the highest close since, and the 50 SMA (160.74) sits on precisely the same price. That confluence (unfilled gap ceiling + 50 SMA + Bollinger upper band 166.38) is the hardest resistance band on the chart.

**Why this matters:** a high-volume gap that is only 40% repaired and never reclaimed is a distribution signature, not a washout. All subsequent rallies have been capped progressively lower (151.50 → 136.27 → 108.78), which is exactly what the 10 EMA sequence shows: 154.86 (11-04) → 142.34 (11-11) → 131.08 (11-17) → 115.11 (11-24).

---

### 5. Momentum: oversold, but with **no** bullish divergence yet

This is the crux, and the nuance most traders get wrong here.

**RSI (14):** 27.32. It has printed below 40 on **every session since 2026-10-30** (31.91) — 17 consecutive sessions, including sub-30 readings on 11-02 (29.70), 11-16 (29.23), 11-17 (27.44), 11-18 (25.84), 11-19 (25.26), **11-20 (22.94 — the most extreme reading in my entire retrieved RSI history back to late June 2026)**, 11-23 (29.80), 11-24 (27.32).

Crucially, RSI made **lower lows alongside lower price lows**: 32.43 (11-13, close 127.65) → 29.23 (11-16, 119.84) → 25.84 (11-18, 110.51) → 22.94 (11-20, 101.97). That is momentum **confirming** the trend, not diverging from it. In a strong downtrend RSI simply stays pinned — exactly the caveat built into the indicator's usage notes. The only softening sign is that on 11-20 → 11-24 price made a marginal new low (intraday 101.71 vs 101.97 close base) while RSI held 27.32 > 22.94, i.e. the last two sessions have *not* produced a new RSI low. That is a **first-order hint** of deceleration, not a divergence, and one weekend-adjacent bounce (11-23, +6.7%) is not a pattern.

**MACD:** line −16.15 vs signal −14.26 → bearish positioning intact. But note the internal conflict:
- The **MACD line made its most negative reading of the entire series today** (−16.1457 vs −15.8914 on 11-20) — trend momentum is still *deteriorating*.
- The **histogram improved two sessions running**: −2.6190 (11-20) → −2.0600 (11-23) → −1.8867 (11-24).

Interpretation: the histogram is contracting because the signal line (an EMA of MACD) is collapsing toward the MACD line, not because price has turned. This is the classic *pre-stabilization* fingerprint — it typically precedes a two-to-five-day technical bounce while leaving the primary downtrend intact. **Treat it as fuel for a short squeeze, not as a trend reversal signal.** For a genuine turn we need the MACD line itself to curl up and cross above the signal (macdh turning positive).

---

### 6. Volatility & band geometry: the squeeze risk is real

- **Band width** = 166.38 − 93.91 = **72.47, i.e. 55.7% of the 130.15 mid-band** — an extremely expanded envelope.
- **%B** = (102.35 − 93.91) / 72.47 = **0.116 (11.6th percentile of the band)** — deep in the lower channel.
- **Yet price has never closed below the lower band** in the retrieved window: 11-20 close 101.97 vs lb 99.41; 11-24 close 102.35 vs lb 93.91. This is a **"band walk"** — the most durable form of downtrend, where price grinds down *alongside* the lower band while the band itself reprices lower (lb fell 149.81 → 93.91, a −37% shift, between 10-30 and 11-24). A band walk warns explicitly against fading the tape purely on "oversold" grounds.
- **ATR 8.91 = 8.71% of price**, but **ATR is declining** from 11.06 (11-05) and 11.55 (10-02) — −19.4% from the 11-05 peak. Volatility is compressing *while price keeps falling*, which is the set-up for either (a) a violent mean-reversion snap toward the mid-band, or (b) a low-volatility base formation. A daily 9-point range is still the base expectation.
- **Today's candle is the worst possible shape:** open = high = 107.49, close 102.35, i.e. the session opened at its peak and never traded above the open, closing 0.4% above the 11-20 low. Zero intraday conviction from buyers.

---

### 7. Volume / supply: heavy overhead inventory

- **VWMA (20d) 121.39 vs close 102.35 → price is 15.7% below its volume-weighted average.** The average holder of traded volume over the last month is deeply underwater, which is precisely the condition that makes rallies into 115–125 get sold (break-even selling).
- Distribution-sized volume clustered on down days: 20.89M (10-30), 14.19M (11-20), 12.55M (11-05), 11.23M (11-16), 10.80M (11-23), 10.68M (11-03). November average ≈ 9.1M.
- **Failed-bounce evidence:** the two-day recovery 11-03 → 11-04 (137.83 → 151.50, +9.9%) was erased in one session on 11-05 (−9.7% to 136.82) on 12.55M shares. That is a *trapped-long cohort at ~150* which now constitutes sell pressure on any retest.
- **Caveat on today's volume:** 7,193,892 is the only volume figure in the entire retrieved series that is not a round multiple of 100, and it is ~21% below the November average despite a −5.9% close. This is consistent with a **partial/intraday snapshot rather than a settled session**. I would not read "declining volume on a down day = seller exhaustion" from it until the session closes.

---

### 8. Level map (all levels derived from concrete dated tool data)

---

### 9. Actionable framework

**Regime call: primary downtrend, overextended but not yet reversing. Bias = short/flat until proven otherwise.** The toolset's trend layer (inverted MA stack, fresh death cross, band walk, price below VWMA) outright overrides the momentum layer's "oversold" flag. RSI at 27 with no divergence and a MACD line at a series low is *evidence of trend strength*, not of an imminent bottom.

1. **Do not buy the dip on RSI alone.** 17 consecutive sub-40 sessions demonstrate the threshold has no reversal power here yet. The minimum viable long trigger is: **close back above the 10 EMA (115.11) on above-average (>9M) volume, with macdh crossing positive.** Anything less is a countertrend scalp inside an active downtrend.
2. **Preferred short structure (risk-defined):** fade rallies into the **108.8–115.1** band (today's failed-bounce high → 10 EMA), invalidation on a close above **VWMA 121.39**. This offers a tight stop in a wide-volatility tape, which is the only sane way to be short here. Do not chase at spot after a −5.9% close with the histogram contracting.
3. **If you must take a mean-reversion long**, treat the mid-band reversion (130.15, +27% from spot) as the target and size it against structure, not conviction: entry near a **held** 101.71–102.35 zone, stop below the **93.91** lower band. Risk ≈ 8.4 points on a 102.35 entry (8.2%); reward to 115.11 ≈ 12.8 points → **~1.5:1**, which is poor. Reward to 130.15 → ~3.3:1 but requires a trend-day that has not yet appeared. **Conclusion: the long is only worth taking with confirmation that lifts the win rate, i.e. after the 10 EMA reclaim.**
4. **Position sizing / risk (mandatory given ATR 8.91):** expect ~9-point daily swings. Halve normal notional; a 1× ATR stop from spot (≈93.4) is a legitimate *close-out* but is not a "tight" stop — it will be hit by noise in a band walk. Use 1.5× ATR (~13.4) below an entry for a swing, and size so the 8.7%-per-day move is within tolerance.
5. **Catalyst awareness / data gap:** the 2026-10-30 gap on the largest volume in the series (20.89M) has the signature of a company-specific repricing event, but **my tools return only price, volume and technicals — no news, filings, or fundamentals field.** The cause is not verifiable here, and neither is the dominant driver for this issuer (a financial-services/crypto-exchange business, whose realized volatility here far exceeds ordinary equity levels). Any factor outside the tape is out of scope for this analysis and is a live risk to all technical levels above.
6. **What would change the call (checklist, in order):** (i) macdh turns positive → squeeze; (ii) close > 115.11 → tactical trend change; (iii) close > 130.15 (20 SMA) *and* 50 SMA slope flattens → intermediate trend change; (iv) 50 SMA back above 200 SMA → strategic trend change. Nothing on today's tape satisfies even (i) with confidence.

# COIN Sentiment Report — 2026-11-17 to 2026-11-24

## 1. Source-by-source breakdown

### News headlines — unavailable
The Yahoo Finance news feed returned: `DATA_UNAVAILABLE: no configured vendor could serve get_news right now (Yahoo Finance request failed: YFDataException)`. ### StockTwits — bearish retail tone, weak bullish base
StockTwits is the only usable source. The screened feed contains **22 on-topic messages** out of 30 fetched. Two different sentiment readings are provided:

- **Explicit user labels:** Bullish 2, Bearish 3, Unlabeled 17.
- **Classifier stance on all on-topic posts:** Bullish 2, Bearish 8, Neutral 5, Unclear 7.

The classifier is more informative here because many posts without labels are clearly negative in body text. The bullish/bearish split is roughly **20% bullish vs 80% bearish among directional classified posts**, or **2/22 bullish vs 8/22 bearish on the full sample**. More importantly, the message content leans negative: several posts describe deep drawdowns, support failure, management distrust, regulatory dependency, and capitulative language.

**Bearish evidence:**
- `@spytrade`: “$COIN -77% from the top.” — drawdown framing.
- `@Barkee`: “down 50% in 6 months, 75% in a year” — trend deterioration.
- `@TheTurdFlusher`: “should find some support in the 70’s” — downside price reference.
- `@Enjoy_Life_Bro`: “60s soon” — bearish price expectation.
- `@DoomBot1`: “BTC freefall to 20k starting. COIN PT 30… Crypto brokers are done.” — extreme bearish thesis tied to crypto weakness.

- `@The_Harmonist` also frames COIN as a macro-sensitive trade: “buyer here, core PCE will come in lower imo tomorrow,” dependent on inflation data and tariff headlines not worsening. This is event-driven, not a durable bullish thesis.

**Neutral or informational evidence:**
- `@GTA_Terminal` reports dark-pool activity: 3.7M shares of COIN traded in dark pools on Monday, Nov 23, about 1.0x the usual amount and 34.1% of volume; the post describes it as neutral. This may indicate non-exchange liquidity but does not by itself signal direction.
- `@GTA_Terminal` also reports Nov 24 options flow: a large put block expiring January 2029 and total premium around $15.0M across about 34,000 contracts “split close to evenly,” with COIN at $103 and down 5.7%. The exact 370-strike put detail is unusual relative to the quoted share price and lacks fuller context, so it should be treated cautiously. The author labels the overall options flow neutral.
- `@openclassaction2` mentions final approval of a $2.25 million Coinbase Dogecoin sweepstakes settlement. This appears to be a localized legal/promo item rather than a dominant market driver based on the available feed.

### Reddit — unavailable
The Reddit fetch failed for r/wallstreetbets, r/stocks, and r/investing. This is **not an absence of discussion**; it is a missing data source. Therefore, no longer-term or community-contrarian sentiment could be compared against StockTwits.

The main divergence is **within StockTwits itself**: explicit user tags are only mildly bearish (2 bullish vs 3 bearish), while the classifier and the message bodies are materially more bearish (8 bearish vs 2 bullish). This suggests users may be withholding labels or posting descriptive negative commentary rather than explicitly marking bearish.

There is **no meaningful cross-source confirmation** from news or Reddit because both are unavailable. As a result, the bearish read rests primarily on retail social tone and observed price/drawdown language. It is useful signal, but it should not be treated as a complete institutional sentiment picture.

## 3. Dominant narrative themes
1. **Drawdown capitulation:** repeated references to COIN being down sharply from highs and prior periods dominate the tone.
2. **Management credibility problem:** complaints about Brian Armstrong, calls for a new CEO, and “torture device” framing indicate negative trust in leadership.
3. **Regulatory dependency:** multiple posts tie COIN’s investability to crypto regulation, suggesting the market may not award a durable premium without clearer rules.
4. **Macro sensitivity:** bullish posts are largely conditional on lower core PCE and absence of adverse tariff news, making sentiment fragile and event-dependent.
5. **Weak retail participation:** one post argues retail investors lack capital and fear getting burned, implying a thin natural bid unless a large catalyst appears.
6. **Liquidity opacity:** dark-pool volume and a large options block introduce uncertainty around whether trading pressure is being shown fully on exchange.

## 4. Catalysts and risks surfaced by the data
**Catalysts:**
- Core PCE data referenced by a bullish trader as a near-term swing factor for COIN.
- Potential tariff-related market reaction; absence of adverse tariff headlines was cited as important.
- Regulatory clarity for crypto, framed by bearish posts as a necessary condition for COIN to be taken seriously.
- Speculative M&A or large corporate news was mentioned as potentially needed to overcome retail distrust, but no confirmed event was provided.
- Options and dark-pool flow could create short-term price dynamics, but direction was reported as neutral or unclear.

**Risks:**
- Continued crypto weakness, especially BTC, was explicitly tied to COIN downside by one bearish poster.
- Support levels cited by users include the 70s, 60s, and an extreme 30 price target, but these are opinions, not validated technicals.
- Management and governance distrust could suppress multiple expansion.
- Retail exhaustion could limit natural buying demand.
- Regulatory uncertainty remains a gating issue in the retail narrative.
- Data quality is impaired because news and Reddit are unavailable, and one options-flow detail appears difficult to interpret without fuller contract information.

| Regulatory dependency | Bearish | StockTwits | “no one is going to take this trash seriously until they regulate crypto” |

## 6. Conclusion for the trader
For **COIN**, the available StockTwits signal is **bearish**: classified bearish posts outnumber bullish posts roughly 4-to-1, the message tone is dominated by drawdown, governance, regulatory, and retail-apathy concerns, and the only bullish posts are short-dated tactical options trades conditional on macro data.
